summary: Some lost things have no sign to show who owns them, so the finder may keep them. Rabbi Meir lists them; Rabbi Yehuda says anything with something unusual about it must be announced.

chunks.en: Which found things belong to the finder,
chunks.st: In a case where one discovers lost items, which found items belong to him,

chunks.en: and which must he announce?
chunks.explain: He tells people he found it so the owner can come.
chunks.st: and for which items is one obligated to proclaim
chunks.stMore: his find so that the owner of the lost items can come and reclaim them?

chunks.en: These found things belong to him:
chunks.st: These found items belong to him:

chunks.en: if he found fruit scattered around,
chunks.st: If one found scattered produce,

chunks.en: coins scattered around,
chunks.st: scattered coins,

chunks.en: bundles of grain in a public place,
chunks.st: bundles of grain in a public area,

chunks.en: round cakes of pressed figs,
chunks.st: round cakes of pressed figs,

chunks.en: loaves of bread from a baker,
chunks.st: baker’s loaves,

chunks.en: strings of fish,
chunks.st: strings of fish,

chunks.en: pieces of meat,
chunks.st: cuts of meat,

chunks.en: wool just sheared, as it comes from its land,
chunks.st: unprocessed wool fleeces that are taken from their state of origin directly after shearing,

chunks.en: bundles of flax,
chunks.st: bound flax stalks,

chunks.en: or strips of purple wool.
chunks.st: or bound strips of combed purple wool,

chunks.en: All these belong to him.
chunks.st: these belong to him,
chunks.stMore: as they have no distinguishing marks that would enable their owners to claim them.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: anything that has something unusual about it
chunks.st: If one finds any lost item in which there is an alteration,

chunks.en: must be announced.
chunks.st: he is obligated to proclaim his find.

chunks.en: How so? If he found a fig cake with a piece of clay inside it,
chunks.st: How so? If he found a round cake of pressed figs with an earthenware shard inside it

chunks.en: or a loaf with coins inside it.
chunks.explain: The owner may have put it there as a sign.
chunks.st: or a loaf of bread with coins inside it,
chunks.stMore: he is obligated to proclaim his find, as perhaps the owner of the item inserted them as a distinguishing mark by means of which he could reclaim his property in case it became lost.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

chunks.he: כָּל כְּלֵי אֶנְפּוֹרְיָא אֵינוֹ חַיָּב לְהַכְרִיז:
chunks.en: new store-bought vessels that all look the same do not need to be announced.
chunks.st: If one finds any anpurya vessels, since their shape is uniform and they are indistinguishable, he is not obligated to proclaim his find.

summary: These are lost things that have a sign or a special spot, so the finder must announce them and give them back.

chunks.en: And these he must announce:
chunks.st: And for these found items, one is obligated to proclaim his find:

chunks.en: if he found fruit in a vessel,
chunks.st: If one found produce inside a vessel,

chunks.en: or a vessel by itself,
chunks.st: or a vessel by itself;

chunks.he: מָעוֹת בְּכִיס אוֹ כִיס כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא,
chunks.en: coins in a purse, or a purse by itself,
chunks.st: coins inside a pouch, or a pouch by itself;

chunks.en: piles of fruit,
chunks.st: piles of produce;

chunks.en: piles of coins,
chunks.st: piles of coins,

chunks.he: שְׁלשָׁה מַטְבְּעוֹת זֶה עַל גַּב זֶה,
chunks.en: three coins one on top of the other,
chunks.st: three coins stacked one atop another;

chunks.en: bundles of grain in a private place,
chunks.st: bundles of grain in a secluded area;

chunks.en: loaves baked at home,
chunks.explain: Each family shapes its bread its own way.
chunks.st: loaves of a homeowner, as each shapes his loaves in his own unique manner;

chunks.en: wool taken from a craftsman's shop,
chunks.st: wool fleeces that are taken from the house of a craftsman, as each craftsman processes the wool in his own unique manner;

chunks.en: jugs of wine and jugs of oil.
chunks.st: jugs of wine; or jugs of oil.

chunks.en: All these he must announce.
chunks.st: If one finds any of these, he is obligated to proclaim his find.

summary: Things that someone left on purpose should not be touched. The mishnah also teaches who owns things found in rubble, in a wall, or in a house that is rented out.

chunks.en: If he found behind a wooden fence,
chunks.st: If one found, behind a wooden fence

chunks.en: or behind a stone wall,
chunks.st: or behind a stone fence,

chunks.en: baby birds tied together,
chunks.st: bound fledglings,

chunks.en: or in the paths in the fields,
chunks.st: or if he found them in the paths that run through fields,

chunks.en: he should not touch them.
chunks.explain: Someone put them there on purpose.
chunks.st: he may not touch them, as they were certainly placed there intentionally.

chunks.en: If he found a vessel in a garbage pile,
chunks.st: In a case where one found a vessel in a garbage dump,

chunks.en: if it is covered,
chunks.st: if it is concealed,

chunks.en: he should not touch it.
chunks.st: he may not touch it, as a person certainly concealed it there.

chunks.en: If it is uncovered,
chunks.st: If it is exposed,

chunks.en: he takes it and announces it.
chunks.st: the finder takes the item and proclaims his find.

chunks.en: If he found things in a pile of stones or in an old wall,
chunks.st: If one found lost items in a heap of stone rubble or in an old wall,

chunks.en: they belong to him.
chunks.st: these belong to him.

chunks.en: If he found them in a new wall,
chunks.st: If one found lost items in a new wall

chunks.en: from the middle outward, they are his;
chunks.st: from its midpoint and outward, they belong to him.

chunks.en: from the middle inward,
chunks.st: If he found the items from its midpoint and inward,

chunks.en: they belong to the owner of the house.
chunks.st: they belong to the homeowner.

chunks.en: If he used to rent the house out to others,
chunks.st: If the homeowner would rent the house to others on a regular basis and there was a steady turnover of residents,

chunks.en: even inside the house,
chunks.st: even if one found lost items inside the house,

chunks.en: they belong to the finder.
chunks.st: these belong to him.
chunks.stMore: Since the owner of the lost items cannot be identified based on location, he will certainly despair of recovering his lost items.

summary: Who keeps money found in a store or at a money changer's table depends on where it was found. Coins found inside fruit someone bought belong to the buyer, unless they were tied up.

chunks.en: If he found something in a store,
chunks.st: If one found items without a distinguishing mark in a store,

chunks.en: it belongs to him.
chunks.st: those items belong to him,
chunks.stMore: as, since the store is frequented by the multitudes, the owner despairs of its recovery.

chunks.en: If it was between the counter and the storekeeper,
chunks.st: If the items were found between the storekeeper’s counter and the storekeeper,

chunks.en: it belongs to the storekeeper.
chunks.st: the items belong to the storekeeper;
chunks.stMore: since his customers do not typically have access to that area, presumably the items are his.

chunks.en: If he found coins in front of a money changer,
chunks.explain: A money changer swaps one kind of coin for another.
chunks.st: If one found coins before a money changer,

chunks.en: they belong to him.
chunks.st: those coins belong to him.

chunks.en: If they were between the chair and the money changer,
chunks.st: If the coins were found between the money changer’s chair and the money changer,

chunks.en: they belong to the money changer.
chunks.st: those coins belong to the money changer, because his clients do not typically have access to that area.

chunks.en: If someone buys fruit from his friend, or
chunks.st: In the case of one who purchases produce from another or in a case

chunks.en: his friend sent him fruit,
chunks.st: where another sent him produce as a gift,

chunks.en: and he found coins in it,
chunks.st: and he found coins intermingled with the produce,

chunks.en: they belong to him.
chunks.st: those coins belong to him.

chunks.en: If the coins were tied up together,
chunks.st: If the coins were bundled,

chunks.en: he takes them and announces them.
chunks.st: this serves as a distinguishing mark and the finder takes the coins and proclaims his find.

summary: The Torah mentions a garment among lost things to teach a rule: anything that has signs and an owner who will look for it must be announced.
stIntro: This mishna is an excerpt from a halakhic midrash concerning lost items, based on the verse: “You shall not see your brother’s ox or his sheep wandering, and disregard them; you shall return them to your brother…And so shall you do with his donkey; and so shall you do with his garment; and so shall you do with every lost item of your brother, which shall be lost from him, and you have found it; you may not disregard it” (Deuteronomy 22:1, 3).

chunks.he: אַף הַשִּׂמְלָה הָיְתָה בִכְלָל כָּל אֵלֶּה.
chunks.en: The garment was also part of the group of all these things.
chunks.explain: The Torah says to return all lost things.
chunks.st: The garment was also included in the generalization that one must return all of these items.

chunks.en: So why was it said by itself?
chunks.st: And why did it emerge from the generalization that is should be specified?

chunks.en: To compare to it,
chunks.st: To draw an analogy to it

chunks.en: to tell you:
chunks.st: and to say to you:

chunks.en: Just as a garment is special because it has
chunks.st: What is notable about a garment?

chunks.en: signs, and someone will look for it,
chunks.st: It is notable in that there are distinguishing marks concerning it and it has claimants asserting ownership, and its finder is obligated to proclaim his find.

chunks.en: so too anything that has
chunks.st: So too with regard to any item concerning which there are distinguishing marks and it has

chunks.en: signs, and someone will look for it,
chunks.st: claimants asserting ownership, its finder is

chunks.en: must be announced.
chunks.st: obligated to proclaim his find.

summary: How long must a finder keep announcing? Rabbi Meir says until his neighbors know of it; Rabbi Yehuda says through three Yamim Tovim and seven days after the last one.

chunks.en: And until when must he announce?
chunks.st: And until when is one who finds a lost item obligated to proclaim his find? He is obligated to do so

chunks.en: Until his neighbors know about it.
chunks.st: until the moment that the neighbors will know of its existence;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: He is obligated to proclaim his find for

chunks.en: Three Yamim Tovim,
chunks.explain: Pesach, Shavuos and Sukkos, when everyone came to Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: three pilgrimage Festivals

chunks.en: and seven days after the last Yom Tov,
chunks.st: and for seven days after the last of the three pilgrimage Festivals,

chunks.en: so that the owner can go home, three days,
chunks.st: so that its owner will have time to go to his home, a trip lasting up to three days, and ascertain that he in fact lost the item,

chunks.en: and come back, three days,
chunks.st: and he will return to Jerusalem, a trip lasting up to three days,

chunks.en: and announce his loss for one day.
chunks.st: and proclaim his loss for one day.

summary: A finder gives a lost thing back only to someone who tells its signs, and not to a cheater. The mishnah teaches what to do with a found animal, and what happens with money from selling it.

chunks.he: אָמַר אֶת הָאֲבֵדָה וְלֹא אָמַר סִימָנֶיהָ,
chunks.en: If someone said what the lost thing was but did not say its signs,
chunks.st: If a claimant accurately stated what type of item the lost item that was found by another is, but did not state, i.e., describe, its distinguishing marks,

chunks.en: he should not give it to him.
chunks.st: the finder shall not give it to him.

chunks.he: וְהָרַמַּאי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר סִימָנֶיהָ,
chunks.en: And a cheater, even though he said its signs,
chunks.st: And in the case of a swindler, even though he stated its distinguishing marks,

chunks.en: he should not give it to him,
chunks.st: the finder shall not give the lost item to him,

chunks.en: as it says in the Torah,
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “And if your brother be not near you, and you know him not, then you shall bring it into your house, and it shall be with you

chunks.en: "Until your brother asks for it."
chunks.st: until your brother claims [derosh] it [oto],
chunks.stMore: and you shall return it to him” (Deuteronomy 22:2). Would it enter your mind that the finder would give it to him before he claims it? How can the finder return it if he does not know the identity of the owner? Rather, the verb derosh is not referring to the claim of the owner; it is referring to the scrutiny performed by the finder.

chunks.en: This means: until you check your brother
chunks.st: You shall not return the lost item until you scrutinize [shetidrosh] your brother to determine

chunks.he: אִם רַמַּאי הוּא אִם אֵינוֹ רַמָּאי.
chunks.en: whether he is a cheater or not a cheater.
chunks.st: whether he, the claimant, is a swindler or whether he is not a swindler.

chunks.en: Any animal that works and eats
chunks.st: If one finds any living being that works and generates enough revenue to cover the costs of the food that it eats, it

chunks.en: should work and eat.
chunks.explain: Its work pays for its food.
chunks.st: shall work and eat while in the finder’s possession.

chunks.en: But an animal that does not work and only eats
chunks.st: And any living being that does not work but it does eat

chunks.en: should be sold,
chunks.st: shall be sold,

chunks.en: as it says, "And you shall return it to him":
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Then you shall bring it into your house, and it shall be with you until your brother claims it, and you shall return it to him” (Deuteronomy 22:2),

chunks.en: see how you can give it back to him.
chunks.explain: Feeding it too long would eat up all its value.
chunks.st: indicating that the finder must see how best to return it to him.
chunks.stMore: Since the owner must repay the finder for his expenditures, if feeding the animal costs more than its value, the finder’s keep-ing the animal in his possession will prevent the owner from recovering it.

chunks.en: What happens with the money?
chunks.st: What shall be done with the money received from the sale of the animal?

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says: The finder

chunks.en: He may use it.
chunks.st: may use it;

chunks.en: So if it gets lost, he must pay it back.
chunks.st: therefore, if the money is lost, he is liable to pay restitution for it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: He may not use it.
chunks.st: He may not use the money;

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אָבְדוּ אֵינוֹ חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָן:
chunks.en: So if it gets lost, he does not have to pay it back.
chunks.st: therefore, if it is lost, he is not liable to pay restitution for it.

summary: A finder must take care of what he found: he airs out sefarim and clothes, and uses metal vessels a little so they do not spoil. He does not need to pick up things that are beneath his honor to carry.

chunks.en: If he found sefarim,
chunks.st: If one found scrolls,

chunks.en: he reads them once every thirty days.
chunks.explain: Opening them lets in air so they do not get moldy.
chunks.st: he reads them once in thirty days in order to ventilate them and prevent mold.

chunks.en: And if he does not know how to read, he rolls them open and closed.
chunks.st: And if he does not know how to read, he rolls and unrolls them in order to ventilate them.

chunks.en: But he should not learn something new from them,
chunks.st: But he shall not study passages in them for the first time,
chunks.stMore: as he would leave the scroll exposed to the air for a lengthy period, thereby causing damage.

chunks.en: and another person should not read with him.
chunks.st: And another person shall not read the scroll with him,
chunks.stMore: as each might pull it closer to improve his vantage point, which could cause the scroll to tear.

chunks.en: If he found a garment,
chunks.st: If one found a garment,

chunks.en: he shakes it out once every thirty days,
chunks.st: he shakes it once in thirty days,

chunks.en: and spreads it out for its own good,
chunks.st: and he spreads it out for its sake, to ventilate it,

chunks.en: but not to look fancy himself.
chunks.st: but he may not use it as a decoration for his own prestige.

chunks.en: Silver vessels and copper vessels
chunks.st: If one found silver vessels or copper vessels,

chunks.en: he uses for their own good,
chunks.st: he may use them for their own sake to prevent tarnish and rust,

chunks.en: but not so much that he wears them out.
chunks.st: but he may not use them to the extent that he will erode them.

chunks.en: Gold vessels and glass vessels
chunks.st: If he finds gold vessels or glass vessels, which are not ruined by neglect,

chunks.he: לֹא יִגַּע בָּהֶן עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ.
chunks.en: he should not touch until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.st: he may not touch them until Elijah will come and identify the owner.

chunks.en: If he found a sack or a basket,
chunks.st: If a person found a sack or a basket

chunks.en: or anything he would not usually carry,
chunks.st: or any other item that it is not his typical manner to take and carry because it is beneath his dignity,

chunks.en: he does not have to take it.
chunks.st: he shall not take it, as one need not demean himself in order to return a lost item.

summary: An animal is lost only when it looks lost, and one must return it even many times. If returning it costs the finder his work, he gets paid like an idle worker, unless he made a condition before beis din.

chunks.en: What counts as a lost thing?
chunks.st: Which is the item that is considered lost property?

chunks.he: מָצָא חֲמוֹר אוֹ פָרָה רוֹעִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ,
chunks.en: If he found a donkey or a cow eating grass on the road,
chunks.st: If one found a donkey or a cow grazing on the path,

chunks.en: that is not a lost thing.
chunks.explain: The owners are probably close by.
chunks.st: that is not lost property,
chunks.stMore: as presumably the owners are nearby and are aware of the animals’ whereabouts.

chunks.en: A donkey with its saddle and bags flipped over,
chunks.st: If one found a donkey with its accoutrements overturned,

chunks.en: a cow running between the vineyards,
chunks.st: or a cow that ran through the vineyards,

chunks.en: that is a lost thing.
chunks.st: that is lost property.

chunks.en: If he returned it and it ran away,
chunks.st: In a case where one returned the lost animal and it fled, and he again

chunks.en: returned it and it ran away,
chunks.st: returned it and it fled,

chunks.en: even four or five times,
chunks.st: even if this scenario repeats itself four or five times,

chunks.en: he must return it,
chunks.st: he is obligated to return it each time,

chunks.en: as it says, "You shall surely return them."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “You shall not see your brother’s ox or his sheep wandering and disregard them; you shall return them to your brother” (Deuteronomy 22:1).

chunks.en: If he stopped work that would have earned a sela,
chunks.explain: A sela is a silver coin.
chunks.st: If in the course of tending to and returning the lost item, the finder was idle from labor that would have earned him a sela,

chunks.he: לֹא יֹאמַר לוֹ תֶּן לִי סֶלַע,
chunks.en: he cannot say to the owner, "Give me a sela."
chunks.st: he shall not say to the owner of the item: Give me a sela to compensate me for my lost income.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא נוֹתֵן לוֹ שְׂכָרוֹ כְּפוֹעֵל בָּטֵל.
chunks.en: Instead, the owner pays him like a worker who sits idle.
chunks.explain: A worker would take less pay to rest instead.
chunks.st: Rather, the owner gives him his wage as if he were a laborer, a payment that is considerably smaller.

chunks.en: If there is a beis din there,
chunks.st: If there are three men there who can convene as a court,

chunks.en: he makes a condition in front of beis din.
chunks.explain: He says he will return it only for full pay.
chunks.st: he may stipulate before the court
chunks.stMore: that he will undertake to return the item provided that he receives full compensation for lost income.

chunks.en: If there is no beis din there,
chunks.st: If there is no court there

chunks.en: in front of whom can he make a condition?
chunks.st: before whom can he stipulate his condition,

chunks.en: His own comes first.
chunks.st: his financial interests take precedence and he need not return the lost item.

summary: The mishnah teaches when a found animal must be returned, that a father cannot tell his son to break a mitzvah, and the mitzvah to help unload and load an animal under its burden.

chunks.en: If he found it in a stable,
chunks.st: If one found an animal in a stable belonging to its owner,

chunks.en: he does not have to return it.
chunks.st: he is not obligated to return it to its owner.

chunks.en: In a public place,
chunks.st: If he found it in a public area,

chunks.en: he must return it.
chunks.st: he is obligated to return it.

chunks.en: And if it was in a graveyard,
chunks.st: And if the animal was lost in a graveyard and a priest found it,

chunks.en: a Kohen may not become tamei for it.
chunks.explain: A Kohen may not go into a graveyard.
chunks.st: he may not become impure to return it.

chunks.en: If his father told him,
chunks.st: If his father said to him:

chunks.en: "Become tamei," or told him,
chunks.st: Become impure; or in a case where one was obligated to return the animal and his father said to him:

chunks.en: "Do not return it,"
chunks.st: Do not return it,

chunks.en: he should not listen to him.
chunks.explain: We may not break the Torah even to honor a father.
chunks.st: he may not listen to his father, as one may not violate Torah law to honor his father.

chunks.en: If he unloaded and loaded,
chunks.st: If one unloaded a burden from an animal collapsing under its weight and then later loaded it onto the animal,

chunks.en: unloaded and loaded,
chunks.st: and later unloaded and loaded it again,

chunks.en: even four or five times,
chunks.st: even if this scenario repeats itself four or five times,

chunks.en: he must keep helping, as it says, "You shall surely help."
chunks.st: he is obligated to continue unloading and loading, as it is stated: “If you see the donkey of him that hates you collapsed under its burden, you shall forgo passing him by; you shall release it [azov ta’azov]
chunks.stMore: with him” (Exodus 23:5). It is derived from the verse that one is obligated to perform the action as needed, even several times.

chunks.en: If the owner went and sat down and said,
chunks.st: If the owner went, and sat, and said to a passerby:

chunks.en: "Since the mitzvah is on you,
chunks.st: Since there is a mitzva incumbent upon you to unload the burden,

chunks.en: if you want to unload, unload,"
chunks.st: if it is your wish to unload the burden, unload it,

chunks.en: the passerby does not have to, as it says, "with him."
chunks.st: in such a case the passerby is exempt, as it is stated: “You shall release it with him,” with the owner of the animal.

chunks.he: אִם הָיָה זָקֵן אוֹ חוֹלֶה, חַיָּב.
chunks.en: If the owner was old or sick, the passerby must help.
chunks.st: If the failure of the owner to participate in unloading the burden was due to the fact he was old or infirm, the passerby is obligated to unload the burden alone.

chunks.en: It is a mitzvah from the Torah to unload,
chunks.st: There is a mitzva by Torah law to unload a burden,

chunks.en: but not to load.
chunks.st: but there is no mitzva to load it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Also to load.
chunks.st: There is even a mitzva to load the burden.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

chunks.he: אִם הָיָה עָלָיו יָתֵר עַל מַשָּׂאוֹ,
chunks.en: If it had more on it than its proper load,
chunks.st: If there was a burden upon the animal greater than its typical burden,

chunks.en: he does not have to help,
chunks.st: one need not attend to it,

chunks.en: as it says, "under its load,"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Under its burden,” i.e., the obligation is with regard to

chunks.en: a load that it is able to carry.
chunks.st: a burden that the animal can bear.
